headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data-flow from next-ai-draw-io into a non-interactive, local-only cheatsheet agent; other pairwise risks are mostly blocked by B's no-I/O profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can ingest PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and uses MCP/browser-backed workflows, while B is documentation-only with no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or network surfaces. That makes direct injection into B unlikely; the only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or external orchestration not shown here, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-generated text into B as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared message queue or clipboard bridge, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of raw A outputs into B prompts.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions before passing text to B.
Keep B in documentation-only mode with no external connectors.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to A outputs before any handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce a sanitizer between A and B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A handles PDFs, text, images, and diagram files and requests API keys/environment variables; B touches no files and has no network or secret-handling surfaces. With no shared workspace or outbound path on B, leakage from A into B is not a default pathway, though manual transfer of sensitive documents would still expose them.
conditions: IF sensitive A inputs are manually pasted into B, those contents can appear in B outputs.
IF B is wrapped by a separate service that logs prompts centrally, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid sending sensitive PDFs or diagrams from A into B.
Redact secrets before any cross-agent handoff.
Keep B offline and documentation-only.
requires-engineering: separate logging/retention for A and B prompts.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on any handoff channel.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network/browser/MCP capabilities, but B cannot write files, modify git, use MCP, or egress network. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, so concurrent write conflict is not plausible from the documented capabilities.
conditions: IF B is replaced with a version that can write files or modify git, conflict becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator grants B shared mutable storage, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep B read-only.
Do not grant B filesystem or git permissions.
Run A and B in separate workspaces.
requires-engineering: add lock coordination before enabling shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate diagram-related content and B is a content-writing/reference agent, but B has no action-taking authority and no direct I/O surfaces. The main risk is B treating A's output as authoritative text during manual handoff; without an automated pipeline, the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF A's output is pasted into B without verification, B may reproduce errors.
IF B is connected to a downstream publishing system, errors can propagate further.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Ask B to cite source material explicitly.
Keep B disconnected from publishing tools.
requires-engineering: add verification checks against source documents.
requires-engineering: add a review gate before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles PDFs, images, and API keys and may send content to third-party model APIs; B is documentation-only with no data handling or network egress. The pair therefore has a compliance mismatch only if regulated or sensitive documents are routed through A, while B itself adds little additional residency or retention risk.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by A through third-party APIs, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF B is later given access to the same regulated data class, the compliance surface expands.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through A.
Use non-sensitive sample documents for B.
Review vendor terms for A's API providers.
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls.
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads from this pair.
